option_relations.rationale: Lipoblastoma is a rare benign tumor of adipocytic origin, consistent with the description of a well-defined, lobulated, hypodense mass with internal septations and a density similar to subcutaneous fat.
Myxoid liposarcoma is a malignant tumor that does not match the benign characteristics described in the vignette.
Lipoma is a benign tumor, but it does not typically exhibit the internal septations and lobulated appearance described in the vignette.
Teratoma or dermoid cyst is a type of tumor that does not match the description of a fatty-appearing mass with internal septations.
Involuting hemangioma is a vascular lesion that does not match the description of a fatty-appearing mass with internal septations.
Hibernoma is a rare benign tumor of brown fat, but it does not match the description of a well-defined, lobulated, hypodense mass with internal septations.
None is not a valid diagnosis.
